items.title: Meet the SAP HANA Cloud Administration Catalog for SAP Automation Pilot
items.author: dona_pavlova
items.text:
What if every SAP HANA Cloud operation your team handles manually today — starting instances, managing backups, running upgrades, configuring replicas — could be executed, scheduled, and orchestrated automatically? 
 That's exactly what the new SAP HANA Cloud Administration catalog brings to SAP Automation Pilot. The service was already helping teams automate parts of this — lifecycle operations, scheduled tasks, environment-specific scenarios, but never through a single, comprehensive, built-in catalog covering the full spectrum. Now, with 40 ready-to-use commands covering everything from provisioning and configuration to recovery and observability, the full picture is finally in one place, regardless of how your instances are provisioned. 

 Inside the Catalog 

 The SAP HANA Cloud Administration catalog organizes its commands into five operational areas, each covering a distinct dimension of database management: 

 Lifecycle and Configuration covers everything from initial setup to ongoing management: provisioning, starting and stopping, resizing, configuring connections, managing backup settings, and enabling advanced capabilities. Pair these commands with an external trigger, and routine operational tasks run themselves. 
 Upgrades and Snapshots Keeping instances current no longer has to be a manual event. List available upgrade versions, optionally rotate a snapshot as a restore point, and trigger the upgrade — all in one automated flow. Snapshot commands can also be used independently to create, list, rotate, or revert snapshots at any point, giving you a reliable safety net before any significant change. 
 Recovery and Business Continuity Perform point-in-time recovery to any timestamp within your backup retention window, recreate an instance from a backup while optionally changing its availability zone, copy a database to an existing target instance, or use cloning templates to capture and restore complete schema and data. These commands put serious data protection capabilities into automated workflows. 
 High Availability and Disaster Recovery Configure synchronous and asynchronous replicas, manage takeovers with no data loss, and orchestrate failover operations across regions. For teams running mission-critical workloads, this group makes resilience automation possible at exactly the moments when manual steps are most risky. 
 Observability, Connectivity, and Plug-ins Retrieve alert rules and active alerts, pull metric definitions and time-series metric values, access capacity consumption data, manage service bindings, and install or update plug-ins — everything you need to monitor, connect, and extend your SAP HANA Cloud instances programmatically. 
 For documentation, prerequisites, and detailed command descriptions, see SAP HANA Cloud Administration (hanacloud-sapcp) Catalog Documentation . 

 What This Looks Like in Practice 

 The impact is already real. SAP IT has used SAP Automation Pilot to automate 95% of manual SAP HANA Cloud operations across its managed instances — spanning health checks, incident management, large-scale change operations, and migration orchestration. 
 The common thread across every scenario: fewer manual steps, less operational risk, and more time for the work that actually matters. 

 Beyond Individual Commands 

 The SAP HANA Cloud Administration catalog commands don't have to work in isolation. SAP Automation Pilot lets you combine them into multi-step workflows, pair them with schedules, and connect them to external triggers — so what starts as a single command can become a fully automated end-to-end operation. A scheduled upgrade that first creates a snapshot. An alert that triggers a restart. A provisioning request that configures the instance and sets up its bindings in one flow. The catalog is the building block, what you build with it is up to you. 

 Get Started 

 The SAP HANA Cloud Administration catalog is available now in SAP Automation Pilot. Head to your tenant, navigate to Catalogs, and explore the full set of commands. For more information, see SAP HANA Cloud Administration (hanacloud-sapcp) Catalog Documentation . 

 New to these products? 

 SAP Automation Pilot is the cloud automation and orchestration engine on SAP Business Technology Platform. It enables teams to automate, schedule, and orchestrate complex operational workflows — turning sequences of manual steps into reliable, repeatable automated processes. More details about the product can be found at: 

 SAP Automation Pilot Documentation 
 SAP HANA Cloud is SAP's fully managed, cloud-native in-memory database platform, available on SAP Business Technology Platform. It delivers the high-performance data foundation that enterprise applications and analytics depend on, with built-in scalability, resilience, and intelligence. More details about the product can be found at: 

 SAP HANA Cloud Documentation 

 Learn More

 Meet your HANA Cloud Lifecycle Agent enabled by Joule and SAP Automation Pilot

items.title: Joule Studio 2.0 with JEV at the Decision Boundary for Autonomous Enterprise AI Agents
items.author: carlosbasto
items.text:
Before we start: this is an independent technical experiment, not an official SAP recommendation. I use “Joule Studio 2.0” for the generation of Joule Studio used here. The SAP documentation supplied for this implementation describes these pro-code capabilities as Early Adopter Care features; commands, interfaces, and availability may change before general availability. JEV is also a newly released technology. All invoice and vendor data in this demonstration is mocked. Releasing a block makes an invoice eligible for subsequent payment; it does not itself execute a payment. 

 1 What this implementation is trying to solve 
 Agentic AI changes the risk profile of an application as soon as the model can call tools with side effects. Reading an invoice, searching vendor history, or summarizing a mismatch are relatively low-impact operations. Clearing a payment block is different: it changes the state of a financial process and can make an invoice eligible for a later payment run. 
 That is the decision point we’ll explore in this article. We will build a supplier-invoice triage agent using Claude Code, the jl CLI, Joule Studio 2.0, and JEV from TypeSafe AI. The agent gathers evidence and decides how to handle the case. Before its release tool can execute, a Python wrapper checks the evidence again and asks JEV for a constrained decision. 
 The generative model handles the conversation, tool orchestration, and explanation. JEV evaluates the proposed action. Ordinary Python maps the result to execution, review, or denial. This makes the transition from reasoning to business action explicit in the implementation and reduces reliance on unconstrained generative output by restricting the consequential decision to predefined outcomes that are enforced in application code. 

 We will go through the concepts, the development setup, the invoice scenario, and the main pieces of code, then build the solution and inspect its behavior in Joule Studio. 

 2 The technologies behind the implementation 
 2.1 Joule Studio pro-code development and the jl CLI 
 SAP documents pro-code development as a way to build Joule Studio solutions from a local IDE and terminal, using the jl CLI and optionally an AI coding agent. The documented workflow covers intent, requirements, specification, solution generation, testing, and deployment. The resulting solution remains source code that developers can inspect and extend. 
 The CLI connects the local workspace to the Joule Studio landscape. It initializes the coding-agent integration, validates the solution structure, packages the assets, and provides deployment and diagnostic commands. Claude Code works inside that environment to read the platform guidance and implement the solution. 
 There are two separate uses of AI here. Claude Code is the development tool. The deployed invoice agent has its own runtime model configuration, business tools, and execution logic. Claude Code does not become a service inside the deployed agent. 
 For the platform workflow, see SAP’s Create an Agent with the CLI and Pro-Code Workflow . 
 2.2 JEV and TypeSafe System One models 
 TypeSafe AI is the company, JEV is its model, and System One is the model category it introduces. TypeSafe announced JEV on 15 September 2026 as its first public System One model, initially in early access. 
 The design centers on a particular consumer: software. An application supplies state and typed questions, and receives answers that it can use directly in its control flow. For this project, the relevant answer is one of four values: allow , confirm , review , or deny . 
 This is more than asking for a nicely formatted response. In its System One documentation , TypeSafe describes models built for constrained judgments and probabilities, without generating a written explanation. The output space is part of the question definition. The application knows which branches it must handle before making the request. 
 That fits the release tool well. By the time release is proposed, the application has already collected business evidence. It needs a judgment about a specific action, followed by a predictable software response. The agent’s LLM remains responsible for explaining the case to the user. 
 2.3 The three TypeSafe primitives 
 TypeSafe exposes three primitives. The introduction and the individual primitive documentation explain their contracts. 

 Primitive 
 What it asks 
 What code receives 

 Choice 
 Which predefined option applies 
 A choice, probabilities, and confidence 

 Score 
 Where the state falls on an ordered rubric 
 A score, probabilities, and confidence 

 Noul 
 Whether a proposition is true 
 A value from 0 to 1 

 Choice naturally fits routing and branching. Score supports ranking or threshold-based behavior. Noul provides a probabilistic answer to a yes/no-style question. In this agent’s running request path, the release guard and completion check both use Choice. 
 The TypeSafe name should not be read as a guarantee of a correct business decision. A constrained answer can still be wrong. The useful contract is that application code can handle the defined outcomes explicitly, while evaluations determine how well the model judges the underlying cases. 
 2.4 Calibration and structured state 
 TypeSafe calls its training approach Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions , or RLCD. Its launch article describes an architecture and training objective focused on producing decisions with useful uncertainty estimates. 
 For Choice and Score, confidence is derived from the returned probability distribution. It is not simply a verbal claim that the model is certain, and it should not be assumed to equal the probability of the selected option. Noul does not have a separate confidence field. TypeSafe’s confidence documentation explains how applications can use this information to choose between automatic action, additional verification, and human review. 
 Calibration is measured across sets of predictions; it does not guarantee an individual answer. Thresholds therefore need evaluation on the application’s own cases. Later in the walkthrough, we will see that this implementation preserves confidence but does not impose a confidence threshold on release. 
 The other useful concept is state . State can be a string, a JSON object, or an array. It carries the material being evaluated; the question separately defines the judgment requested. JEV currently accepts text and structured text data, not invoice images. See TypeSafe’s State documentation . 
 In our implementation, that state describes the proposed tool call, its arguments, evidence summaries, policy, side effects, and reversibility. JEV does not connect to SAP to discover these facts. Our application supplies them. 
 2.5 Small judgments composed in software 
 TypeSafe recommends narrowly scoped questions and composition in code. Independent questions can share one state in a batched request, but one answer does not automatically become the input to another question in that batch. 
 Here, the runtime uses one focused release question after Python has assembled the risk context. This is a practical entry point for experimenting with System One models inside an agent: a named action, a defined answer space, and explicit consequences for every answer. 
 JEV is new enough that I would treat this as an architectural direction to evaluate, rather than a settled standard. What makes it interesting is the possibility of composing specialized model judgments inside ordinary software, while retaining the flexibility of an agent around them. 

 3 Development approach from intent to a Joule Studio solution 
 3.1 Prepare the development environment 
 You need access to a Joule Studio landscape with the relevant pro-code capabilities, a local Claude Code installation, and access to TypeSafe’s API. SAP’s EAC guide specifies Node.js 24 or later for the CLI. The mock scenario does not require a live S/4HANA connection, although the deployed agent still needs its platform-provided runtime model access. 
 Use SAP’s Pro-Code Setup and Anthropic’s Claude Code quickstart for installation and access prerequisites. The EAC CLI installation command in the SAP guide used for this project is: npm install -g @SAP /joule-work-dev-cli-early-adopters@latest
jl v 
 This is an EAC installation pattern, not a promise of a permanently available public npm package. Follow the package access instructions for your landscape and check the current SAP guide before installing. 
 In Joule Studio, open your user settings, go to Develop , and copy the personal Sign-in URL under CLI Authorization . Pass it to the CLI in quotes: jl login '<your Sign-in URL>'
cd supplier-invoice-triage-agent
jl init claude 
 If the folder does not exist yet, then use: mkdir supplier-invoice-triage-agent
cd supplier-invoice-triage-agent
jl init claude 
 jl init claude installs the Joule Studio development skills and creates the MCP configuration used by Claude Code. The coding agent can then work with platform-specific guidance and development tools from this workspace. SAP’s AI Coding Agent documentation explains this integration. 

 3.2 Define the business intent and refine the implementation 
 I used an iterative pro-code workflow. After initializing the workspace, I worked with Claude Code to review and refine the invoice-triage implementation inside the Joule Studio project. The focus was on validating the business behavior, the local test tools, the JEV integration, and the deployable solution structure against the intended design. 
 The implementation starts from a concise business and technical intent: Build a Joule Studio agent that triages a blocked supplier invoice. It must retrieve invoice and matching evidence, check recent invoices from the same vendor, and either release the payment block, create an AP-clerk task, or escalate.

Use local test data for the business tools.

Before any release executes:
- reconstruct the relevant invoice and vendor-history evidence;
- evaluate the proposed release with TypeSafe JEV;
- use a Choice decision with allow, confirm, review, or deny;
- and enforce the result in Python so that only an explicit allow can reach the original release tool. 
 Rather than treating this as a one-shot code-generation exercise, I used Claude Code as a development and review partner. The implementation was inspected against the requirements, with particular attention to the files that define the runtime behavior: 
 app/agent.py 
 app/agent_executor.py 
 app/decision_gates.py 
 app/jev.py 
 app/mcp_providers/agw.py 
 mcp-mock.json 
 asset.yaml 
 solution.yaml 
 The review focuses on a few concrete questions: 
 Does the agent retrieve the invoice and recent vendor history before proposing a release? 
 Is release_payment_block actually wrapped before the agent receives the tool? 
 Does the wrapper reconstruct evidence independently of the LLM reasoning? 
 Is JEV called with the intended allow , confirm , review , and deny decision space? 
 Do missing, failed, disabled, or invalid JEV decisions hold the release instead of allowing it through? 
 Does only an explicit allow invoke the original release coroutine? 
 This is the important part of the pro-code workflow: Claude Code can help generate, inspect, and refine the implementation, but the resulting source remains normal application code that can be reviewed against explicit business and technical requirements. 
 The later sections follow the runtime path in detail and show exactly where these behaviors are implemented. Review this Joule Studio 2.0 invoice-triage agent against the intended implementation below.

Business behavior:
- Triage a blocked supplier invoice using invoice number and fiscal year.
- Retrieve invoice detail and PO / goods-receipt evidence.
- Retrieve recent invoices for the same vendor to identify potential duplicate risk.
- The agent may release the payment block, create an AP-clerk task,

items.title: New ABAP editor in LSMW
items.author: Joris
items.text:
In my old blog 'How to get the new ABAP editor in LSMW' I described how a single enhancement enables the new ABAP editor in SAP's LSMW. While that solution only takes one implicit enhancement spot, it has a few (minor) limitations. In this next blog I will describe another approach to enabling the new ABAP editor in LSMW. This new solution is slightly more invasive, but gives us much more flexibility. 
 The solution 
 This solution involves an enhancement spot and a new function group with a screen. The big advantage of this solution is that almost all limitations of the first approach are gone. Also you will have full control of the screen and its functions. For this implementation I have added a set of much used LSMW functions directly on the toolbar (as buttons). You are free to add, remove, change those to your liking! 

 Features 
 New ABAP editor for all ABAP coding within LSMW (field mappings, events, user defined routines and form routines) 
 Code completion 
 Pretty printer 
 ABAP Syntax checker 
 Use of LSMW-specific inserts (mapping source fields, global variables, global functions) 
 Use of ABAP statement templates 
 Use of (almost) all new-editor features such as Edit buffers, up- and download of source, etc. 
 Automatic use of 72-character version of the new editor, irrespective of your global setting in SE80 
 (Read about the limitation & work around in the previous blog ) 

 Limitations 
 Code completion is not aware of globally defined variables. 
 (It must be possible to also get rid of this limitation, but that is for the community to pick up. look at CL_ABAP_PARSER for starters.) 

 Implementation 

 By far the easiest way to implement is by using SAPlink . This will install the function group, screen and enhancement spot implementation in one go. 

 The implementation comprises 

 A custom function group ZLSMW_NEW_EDITOR with one function module and one screen 
 An implicit enhancement spot at the start of Subroutine EDITOR_START of Function group /SAPDMC/LSMW_AUX_080 
 (optional) A user parameter to switch the solution on or off per user. 

 I added ample comments in the code, so it is easier to understand what is happening. 

 Implementation using SAPlink 
 I will assume you have installed- and are familiar with SAPlink . 
 Install the .NUGG file attached to this post. It will upload and install the following components 
 Development package ZLSMW 
 Function group ZLSMW_NEW_EDITOR 
 Implicit enhancement spot ZLSMW_NEW_EDITOR @ Subroutine EDITOR_START of Function group /SAPDMC/LSMW_AUX_080 
 Check and activate the new objects. You might need to assign them explicitly to the new package ZLSMW (as they all end up in your $TMP) 
 Manually create User Parameter ZLSMW_NEWEDITOR ( how-to , scroll all the way down) and assign the parameter with value 'X' to each user that wants to use the new editor. All other users will not be affected. 
 Done! Start LSMW and check out the new features! 

 Manual implementation 
 Alternatively you can implement it manually; 

 Package ZLSMW 
 Create a development package ZLSMW. Save and activate. 
 Function group ZLSMW_NEW_EDITOR 
 Create function group ZLSMW_NEW_EDITOR and assign it to the newly created package ZLSMW 
 Function module ZCALL_ABAP_EDITOR In the new function group create function module ZCALL_ABAP_EDITOR with the following interface 
 IMPORTING 
 REFERENCE(IV_EDITMODE) TYPE CHAR4 
 CHANGING 
 REFERENCE(CT_SOURCE) TYPE RSWSOURCET For the implementation paste in the FM code from the attached text file code2.txt and save. 

 Include LZLSMW_NEW_EDITORTOP 
 Create a new include called LZLSMW_NEW_EDITORTOP in the function group and paste in the include code from the attached text file code2.txt. The include holds both the global variables, form routines and PAI/PBO Modules. I know, it is not as it should be done, but it limits the number of includes If the new PAI and PBO modules etc do not appear in the SE80 tree you need to rebuild the object list. You do this by right clicking on the function group name in the SE80 tree on the left, then go to Other Functions --> Rebuild Object List. 

 Screen 3000 
 Create a new screen 3000. Add a custom container called EDITOR over the full size of the canvas and save. In the screens flow logic un comment the PAI and PBO modules MODULE STATUS_3000 and MODULE USER_COMMAND_3000. 

 Pf-status EDITOR 
 Copy pf-status EDITOR from function group /SAPDMC/LSMW_AUX_080 to your new function group. Name it also EDITOR. Next you need to remove a few items from the menu bar. Remove the items in yellow: 
 Change the toolbar functions such that it resembles below screenshot. 

 Optionally you can change the function keys to your liking. 

 Enhancement spot 
 Create an Implicit enhancement spot ( how-to ) at the start of Subroutine EDITOR_START of Function group /SAPDMC/LSMW_AUX_080. Paste in the enhancement code from file code2.txt attached to this post & activate. 

 User Parameter 
 Create a user parameter ZLSMW_NEWEDITOR in SE80 ( how-to scroll all the way down). Assign the parameter with value 'X' to each user that wants to use the new editor. All other users will not be affected. This is optional . If you want all users to use the new editor, omit this step and remove the check in the enhancement spot implementation. 

 Done! Activate all and start LSMW. 

 Enjoy! Please let me know of any bugs or shortcomings. 

 Download the ZIP with all code here

items.title: Securing PII in SAP Incentive Management: Implementing Dynamic Data Masking in the EXT Schema
items.author: rudrakumar_puppala
items.text:
Are you storing sensitive PII—such as Social Security Numbers or Credit Card details—in your SAP Incentive Management custom tables? 
 When operating on hyperscalers, keeping this data secure is a top compliance priority. But how do you protect sensitive fields from developers and workflow scripts while still allowing your tenant user to generate reports and encrypted exports? 
 In this post, we break down how to implement SAP HANA Dynamic Data Masking in the EXT schema. Learn how to: 
 Mask sensitive columns on-the-fly using simple SQL masking expressions. 
 Enforce the Principle of Least Privilege by revoking UNMASKED access from WebIDE roles and workflow scripts. 
 Ensure seamless operations by safely granting unmasked access to only authorized tenant users ( G3XX ). 
 Protect your database layer without interrupting your business workflows!

items.title: Vehicle-to-Grid integration in IS-U Billing
items.author: Beaucamp99
items.text:
The Utilities industry is facing an increasing demand for flexible solutions to manage Distributed Energy Resources (DER), driven by the growing adoption of new technologies and commercial offerings for energy consumers. One such scenario is Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G), which is transforming electric vehicles from energy consumers into flexible energy resources. Besides charging and discharging electricity, several utilities and mobility providers are beginning to remunerate customers for keeping their vehicle connected to the grid and available for flexibility services. 
 Inspired by Holger Schweinfurth's Vehicle-to-Grid demonstration, I explored how such a scenario could be implemented using only standard SAP IS-U configuration. This led me to build and test two different scenarios in our SAP S/4HANA system: 

 Besides energy measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh), the V2G model may introduce a second commercial dimension: the time during which a vehicle remains connected and available for grid services. While this duration may be recorded in minutes, a commercial model may remunerate this availability using an hourly rate. 
 In this blog series, we will look at the customizing requirements needed not only to capture Meter Reading (MR) results recorded in kilowatt-hours (kWh), but also to capture the time a vehicle remains connected to the grid in minutes (MIN) and subsequently use this information for billing. 
 This reflects an emerging commercial model in which customers may receive an availability payment for keeping a compatible EV connected and available for grid services. 
 It is important to bear in mind that this blog series does not describe a complete V2G solution or the technical integration between an EV, charging infrastructure, energy management system and utility backend. Instead, it focuses specifically on how standard SAP IS-U device and billing configuration can be used to model and bill selected V2G-related quantities. 
 Furthermore, we will also have a closer look on how IS-U rates can be configured to allow the billing and invoicing of MR Results registered in both kWh and MIN. 
 As a final addition to this blog series, there will be a final part on how the Convergent Invoicing (CI) component of Billing and Revenue Innovation Management (BRIM) could be leveraged to calculate an availability bonus for a customer without directly maintaining the entire V2G set-up in IS-U. 
 By the end of this blog series, you will have an end-to-end example showing how standard SAP IS-U can bill: 
 energy imported from the grid (kWh), 
 energy exported back to the grid (kWh), and 
 availability time, measured in minutes and remunerated in hours, 
 using only standard SAP IS-U configuration and billing functionality. To top it all off, you will also have seen a possible strategy through which the availability bonus could be applied by integrating CI in IS-U billing. 

 Part 1: Business context and device/register configuration 
 This first part of this series will be dedicated to the set-up of two IS-U Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) installations. In this example, the V2G scenario is represented through three commercially relevant quantities: energy consumed while charging, energy exported while discharging, and the time during which the vehicle remains connected and available for grid services. To represent these requirements, two scenarios were built in our SAP S/4HANA system. 
 The first scenario uses a single device with three registers. Two registers measure the energy consumed during charging and exported during discharging in kWh, while the third register measures the time the vehicle remains connected to the grid in minutes (MIN). The second scenario uses two separate devices: one for the energy quantities measured in kWh and another for the connection time measured in MIN. 
 The image of the data environment below gives an overview of the set-up in our SAP S/4HANA system. 

 Assuming your SAP system already has an adequate material (MM) configured to allow the creation of electricity meters in SAP IS-U, a new register group will have to be configured to capture the MR results both KWH and MIN. 
 This can be achieved by simply using transaction EG04 or by navigating through the SAP MENU as illustrated below: 
 SAP MENU >> Device Management >> Technology >> Register Group >> EG04: Create 
 In this example Register Group E_V2G was created to meet the business requirement for the first scenario. Two registers measuring the consumption in KWH and a third one measuring the time connected to the grid in MIN: 

 For the second scenario, which uses two separate devices, the E_V2G register group was used as a template to create two dedicated register groups 
 1. E_V2GC – Register group for device exclusively measuring in kWh 

 2. E_V2GT – Register group for device exclusively measuring in MIN 

 Since MIN is not the typical unit used for an electricity register, an additional configuration step is required before it can be assigned to the register category. The relevant division and register categories must be linked to the dimension containing the UoM MIN. 
 Register group E_V2G – Register categories. 

 This can be achieved using the following customizing path: 
 SAP Customizing Implementation Guide >> SAP Utilities >> Device Management >> Technology >> Register Group >> Allocate Units of Measurement to Register Categories 

 Table T006 allows you to easily verify to which dimension(s) the required UoM(s) belong(s): 
 Link between UoM and Dimension in table T006 . 

 This can also be verified by navigating through the following customizing path: 
 SAP Customizing Implementation Guide >> ABAP Platform >> General Settings >> Check Units of Measurement 

 Once the register group has been configured in line with the business requirement, the devices can be created with the newly created register groups: 
 ISU-EWALLBOX with register group E_V2G. 

 ISU-WALLBOX with register group E_V2GC. 

 1 with register group E_V2GT. 

 The next step would be to first technically install the devices and then realize the billing relevant installation in the IS-U installation provided for this use case. 
 Scenario 1: 
 Device ISU-EWALLBOX installed in installation 4100000512. 

 Rate data of installation 4100000512. 

 Scenario 2: 
 Device ISU-WALLBOX in conjunction with device 1 installed in installation 4100000513. 

 Rate data of installation 4100000513. 

 Before the billing-relevant installation of the device can be realized, the IS-U rates required to register the consumptions must already be configured for the installations concerned. In addition, the rate determination linking the rate category to the active rates through a rate type will also be required. These topics will be covered in the next part of this blogging series, where we will take a closer look at the rate and operand configuration and explore some of the more interesting aspects of the V2G billing scenario. 
 Over the next few weeks, the following blog posts will be published: 
 Part 2: From Meter Reading Results to Billable Quantities 
 Part 3: From Measured Quantities to Billing and Invoicing 
 Part 4: Integration in Billing and Revenue Innovation Management (BRIM) for calculation of availability bonus

items.title: How We Built a Learning Assignment Management Solution for SAP SuccessFactors HCM Using SAP BAIP
items.author: KavyaManohara
items.text:
Introduction 
 Managing learning assignments for employees can become complex when managers need to identify the right learning, select employees from their reporting organization, check existing assignment status, submit assignment or removal requests, and track the approval process. 
 To address this, we identified the need for a centralized Learning Assignments Management Solution for SAP SuccessFactors HCM that simplifies the process of assigning and removing learning for employees while providing visibility into requests, approvals, assignment status, and learning-related analytics. 
 The solution provides managers with a structured application to discover learning, manage assignments for their reporting employees, submit requests, track approvals, and analyze learning assignment data through a centralized interface. 
 Our Approach 
 We built a Learning Assignments Management Solution for SAP SuccessFactors HCM on SAP BAIP to simplify and streamline the manager-driven learning assignment process. 
 The solution brings together Learning Catalogue access, Reporting Assignments, learning assignment and removal requests, approval workflows, My Requests, Inbox, notifications, and Analytics & Reporting into a unified application. 
 Managers can select the organization or unit they are responsible for, search for the required learning, view their reporting employees and existing assignment status, select one or multiple employees, and submit a request to assign or remove learning. 
 The request is then routed through the appropriate approval process. Approvers can review requests through their inbox and approve or reject them. Based on the approval decision, the corresponding learning assignment or removal is processed for the selected employees. 

 Key Features and Benefits 
 1. Learning Catalogue 
 Provides managers with a centralized view of available learning items and curricula . 
 Enables managers to search and discover required learning based on their business needs.

items.title: Service Procurement Using Maintenance Plan in SAP PM
items.author: LOURDES_16
items.text:
INTRODUCTION 
 In one of my recent SAP PM projects at a manufacturing plant, we had a recurring requirement that was a good fit for Service Procurement using a Maintenance Plan I would like to share the steps we followed. 
 For example, let’s take a plant which have about 40 elevators and 15 air conditioning units across different buildings. All of these were under Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMC) with external vendors. Every month, the vendor would come and do preventive maintenance, and the plant would get an invoice. The ask was to automatically plan these external services. The solution was to use Maintenance plan for Service Procurement. STEP BY STEP PROCESS FLOW 
 Step: 1 Create a Purchase Contract using ME31K . Maintain the Agreement type, supplier, Purchasing Organization and Purchasing group. Maintain it as Service(D) and Account assignment as F. 
 Step: 2 Create a Maintenance Order in IW31. Enter the required technical object and maintain the Control Key as PM03 for external service. In the Agreement field, enter the Purchase Contract created in Step-1 Release the order and Save. 

 Step 3 Once the order is Released, a Purchase Requisition (PR) is generated automatically. Create a Purchase Order in ME21N by using this PR 

 Step 4 Create a Maintenance Plan in IP01 using the Maintenance Plan Category MM Service Procurement. Enter the Cycle, Unit and Purchase Order created 

 Step 5 Schedule the Maintenance Plan in IP10. Click Start to schedule the plan and Save it 

 Once the plan is Scheduled, Select the line item and click on the display object. A Periodic Service entry sheet will be created automatically. 

 In our case, the Service Entry Sheet (SES) was automatically created by the Maintenance Plan. The only remaining step was to accept the Service Entry Sheet. 
 CONCLUSION 
 By using a Maintenance Plan for Service Procurement, we were able to plan recurring external maintenance services in a structured and automated manner. The process connected the maintenance and procurement activities, from the Purchase Contract and Maintenance Order through to the Purchase Order and Service Entry Sheet. This helped us plan the recurring external maintenance services through the Maintenance Plan and reduce the manual effort involved in creating service-related documents for the planned month.

items.title: Parallelizing BAPI Calls with CL_ABAP_PARALLEL — A QM Performance Story (9 min → 30 sec)
items.author: Mannjuanth
items.text:
SAP ABAP · Performance · Parallel Processing 
 From 10 Minutes to 30 Seconds with CL_ABAP_PARALLEL 
 What happens when a production inspection screen has to read 30+ inspection points — and every point requires its own BAPI call? 
 In our case, the answer was a wait of 6–11 minutes . The data was correct, but the user experience wasn't. 6–11 min Sequential processing → 20–30 sec Parallel processing 
 The key was simple: each inspection point could be read independently. That made the workload a natural fit for SAP's standard CL_ABAP_PARALLEL framework. 
 This post walks through the production design: the orchestrator and task classes, XSTRING data buffers, shared read logic, and — perhaps more importantly — the guardrails around task count, thresholds, timeouts, debugging, memory and error handling . Same data. Same results. A fraction of the waiting time. 
 If you're dealing with a loop of independent, I/O-bound BAPI or RFC calls, this might give you a practical pattern worth stealing.

How can you provide the user with default values in the popup of an action in RAP ? 
 Introduction 
 When a user triggers an action in the Fiori Elements UI, you usually want to have some information from the user. To make life easier for the user, you can also provide default values in many situations so that the user receives suggestions for input and thus works faster. To do this, we will extend our Report Pattern app with another function. 
 Behaviour definition 
 To do this, we have a current definition of the "Approve" action in the behaviour definition. We are currently using a simple action with a parameter, which ensures that a popup is displayed when triggered. 

 To do this, we add DEFAULT FUNCTION in curly brackets to define a new function in which we can set the default values. 
 The name of the function must begin with " GetDefaultsFor " or " GetDfltsFor ". Here you already get the information. managed implementation in class zbp_sm_i_trav_req unique;
strict ( 2 );
with draft;

define behavior for ZSM_I_TRAV_REQ //alias <alias_name>
persistent table zsm_travel_req
draft table zsm_trv_draft
lock master
total etag LastModifiedOn
authorization master ( instance )
//etag master <field_name>
{
 create ( authorization : global );
 update;
 delete;
 field ( readonly, numbering : managed ) RequestId;

 action ( features : instance ) Approve parameter ZA_APPROVE_PARAM
 result [1] $self { default function GetDefaultsFor_Appr; }

 action ( features : instance ) Reject result [1] $self;
 action ( features : instance ) cancel result [1] $self;

 draft action Activate optimized;
 draft action Edit;
 draft action Discard;
 draft action Resume;

 draft determine action Prepare;

 mapping for zsm_travel_req
 {
 RequestId = request_id;
 EmployeeId = employee_id;
 Destination = destination;
 Status = status;
 CreatedBy = created_by;
 CreatedOn = created_on;
 EmployeeName = employee_name;
 LastModifiedBy = last_modified_by;
 LastModifiedOn = last_modified_on;
 TravelDate = travel_date;
 }
} 
 Behaviour implementation 
 If you place the cursor on the name of the function, you can use CTRL + 1 to generate the method in the behaviour implementation. Let's take a look at the signature of the new method. 

 We receive the keys of the currently selected entries and can return our values via RESULT. There, next to the key, you will find the %PARAM field, where our parameter structure is defined. To do this, we define a small logic that defines a default value for Approved date, Approved by and remarks . 
 CLASS lhc_ZSM_I_TRAV_REQ DEFINITION INHERITING FROM cl_abap_behavior_handler.
 PRIVATE SECTION.

 METHODS get_instance_authorizations FOR INSTANCE AUTHORIZATION
 keys REQUEST requested_authorizations FOR zsm_i_trav_req RESULT result.

 METHODS get_global_authorizations FOR GLOBAL AUTHORIZATION
 REQUEST requested_authorizations FOR zsm_i_trav_req RESULT result.
 METHODS approve FOR MODIFY
 keys FOR ACTION zsm_i_trav_req~approve RESULT result.

 METHODS cancel FOR MODIFY
 keys FOR ACTION zsm_i_trav_req~cancel RESULT result.

 METHODS reject FOR MODIFY
 keys FOR ACTION zsm_i_trav_req~reject RESULT result.
 METHODS get_instance_features FOR INSTANCE FEATURES
 keys REQUEST requested_features FOR zsm_i_trav_req RESULT result.
 METHODS getdefaultsfor_appr FOR READ
 keys FOR FUNCTION zsm_i_trav_req~getdefaultsfor_appr RESULT result.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS lhc_ZSM_I_TRAV_REQ IMPLEMENTATION.

 METHOD get_instance_authorizations.
 ENDMETHOD.

 METHOD get_global_authorizations.
 ENDMETHOD.

 METHOD Approve.
 MODIFY ENTITIES OF zsm_i_trav_req IN LOCAL MODE
 ENTITY zsm_i_trav_req
 UPDATE FIELDS ( Status )
 WITH VALUE #( FOR ls IN keys
 ( %tky = ls-%tky
 Status = 'A - APPROVED' ) ).

 READ ENTITIES OF zsm_i_trav_req IN LOCAL MODE
 ENTITY zsm_i_trav_req
 ALL FIELDS WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
 RESULT DATA(lt_read).

 result = VALUE #( FOR ls1 IN lt_read
 ( %tky = lS1-%tky
 %param = ls1 ) ).
 ENDMETHOD.

 METHOD cancel.
 MODIFY ENTITIES OF zsm_i_trav_req IN LOCAL MODE
 ENTITY zsm_i_trav_req
 UPDATE FIELDS ( Status )
 WITH VALUE #( FOR ls IN keys
 ( %tky = ls-%tky
 Status = 'C - CANCELLED' ) ).

 READ ENTITIES OF zsm_i_trav_req IN LOCAL MODE
 ENTITY zsm_i_trav_req
 ALL FIELDS WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
 RESULT DATA(lt_read).

 result = VALUE #( FOR ls1 IN lt_read
 ( %tky = lS1-%tky
 %param = ls1 ) ).
 ENDMETHOD.

 METHOD Reject.
 MODIFY ENTITIES OF zsm_i_trav_req IN LOCAL MODE
 ENTITY zsm_i_trav_req
 UPDATE FIELDS ( Status )
 WITH VALUE #( FOR ls IN keys
 ( %tky = ls-%tky
 Status = 'R - REJECTED' ) ).

 READ ENTITIES OF zsm_i_trav_req IN LOCAL MODE
 ENTITY zsm_i_trav_req
 ALL FIELDS WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
 RESULT DATA(lt_read).

 result = VALUE #( FOR ls1 IN lt_read
 ( %tky = lS1-%tky
 %param = ls1 ) ).
 ENDMETHOD.

 METHOD get_instance_features.
 READ ENTITIES OF zsm_i_trav_req IN LOCAL MODE
 ENTITY zsm_i_trav_req
 ALL FIELDS WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
 RESULT DATA(lt_read).

 result = VALUE #( FOR ls_read IN lt_read
 ( %key = ls_read-%key
 %features-%action-Approve = COND #( WHEN ls_read-Status = 'A - APPROVED' OR ls_read-Status = 'C - CANCELLED' OR ls_read-Status = 'R - REJECTED'
 THEN if_abap_behv=>fc-o-disabled
 ELSE if_abap_behv=>fc-o-enabled )

 %features-%action-Reject = COND #( WHEN ls_read-Status = 'R - REJECTED' OR ls_read-Status = 'C - CANCELLED' OR ls_read-Status = 'A - APPROVED'
 THEN if_abap_behv=>fc-o-disabled
 ELSE if_abap_behv=>fc-o-enabled )

 %features-%action-cancel = COND #( WHEN ls_read-Status = 'C - CANCELLED' OR ls_read-Status = 'R - REJECTED' OR ls_read-Status = 'A - APPROVED'
 THEN if_abap_behv=>fc-o-disabled
 ELSE if_abap_behv=>fc-o-enabled ) ) ).
 ENDMETHOD.

 METHOD GetDefaultsFor_Appr.

 LOOP AT keys INTO DATA(ls_keys).
 INSERT VALUE #( %tky = ls_keys-%tky
 %param = VALUE za_approve_param( ApprovalDate = cl_abap_context_info=>get_system_date( )
 Remarks = 'Leave Remarks here'
 ApprovedBy = cl_abap_context_info=>get_user_technical_name( ) ) ) INTO TABLE result.

 ENDLOOP.
 ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS. 
 Projection 
 Now comes the most important step. So that the function can be called from the frontend, we have to release it in the projection of our RAP object to the outside. In this case, it is not an action, but a function. Accordingly, the implementation looks like this: 

 Test 
 Now that we have everything prepared, we can carry out the test in application. To do this, we click on Approve and trigger the action. You can see the result. 

 Conclusion 
 Using Default Functions in RAP is a simple and effective way to prepopulate action popup fields with meaningful values, such as the current date, logged-in user, or business-specific defaults. This improves usability, reduces manual data entry, and ensures consistent data capture. 
 By defining a DEFAULT FUNCTION , implementing the corresponding GetDefaultsFor_* method, and exposing it in the projection behavior, developers can provide a smarter and more user-friendly Fiori experience with minimal development effort.

items.title: End-to-End API Automation of 5HP Advanced Intercompany Stock Transfer in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public
items.author: Qi_Liu
items.text:
Scope Item: 5HP — Advanced Intercompany Stock Transfer 
 Document Type: NBIC (Cross-Company, Delivery-Linked) 
 Verified on: SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 
 Document chain (example): 
 STO (NBIC)
 └─→ OBD
 ├─→ IV2 (auto-generated after PGI via Output Determination)
 └─→ IBD (auto-generated after PGI)
 └─→ GR Complete 
 1. Why 5HP Is Architecturally Different from Standard Stock Transfers 
 5HP uses the NBIC purchase order type. Three differences that break any assumption carried over from standard NB flows: 

 No direct GR against the PO. The full delivery chain is mandatory — OBD → PGI → IBD → GR. Attempting to post GR directly against the intercompany PO returns error M7/036 . 

 IV2 is auto-generated, not API-driven. After PGI, Output Determination automatically creates the intercompany invoice (IV2). API_BILLING_DOCUMENT_SRV is read-only — there is no API to create IV2, and none is needed. 

 Session-bound ETag on all FunctionImports. Every write operation in API_OUTBOUND_DELIVERY_SRV requires the CSRF token fetch, entity GET, and FunctionImport POST to share the same HTTP session (cookie jar). Stateless calls return 412 or 428. (See SAP Note 3539067.) 
 2. Authentication and Session Architecture 
 All write operations use a Communication User via Basic Auth, provisioned through the relevant Communication Arrangement (e.g., SAP_COM_0106 for Delivery Processing Integration, SAP_COM_0209 for Inbound Delivery). 
 $user = "<comm-user>"
$pass = '<password>'
$base = "https://<your-tenant>.s4hana.cloud.sap"
$cookieJar = "$env:TEMP\obd_cookies_$(Get-Date -Format 'HHmmss').txt" 
 The session rule: Every POST / PATCH / DELETE must use curl -c/-b <cookie-jar> to maintain session continuity across calls. PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest and stateless REST clients do not preserve the server-side session and will fail with CSRF or ETag errors. 
 BTP Integration Suite: Configure a persistent HTTP Receiver Adapter with a Cookie Session Handler policy. The iFlow must model the CSRF token fetch as an explicit preceding step — do not assume the token survives across integration flow restarts or parallel executions. 
 3. Step 1 — Create STO ( ✅ API Verified) 
 Service: api_stocktransportorder (OData V4) 
 Available from: Release 2602 
 Reference: SAP Community — Stock Transport Orders via API in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 
 POST https://<your-tenant>.s4hana.cloud.sap/sap/opu/odata4/sap/api_stocktransportorder/srvd_a2x/sap/stocktransportorder/0001/StockTransportOrder
Content-Type: application/json
x-csrf-token: <fetched-token> 
 Request body: 
 {
 "StockTransportOrderType": "NBIC",
 "CompanyCode": "<receiving-company-code>",
 "PurchasingOrganization": "<purchasing-org>",
 "PurchasingGroup": "<purchasing-group>",
 "SupplyingPlant": "<supplying-plant>",
 "DocumentCurrency": "<currency>",
 "Language": "<language-key>",
 "_StockTransportOrderItem": [
 {
 "StockTransportOrderItem": "00010",
 "Product": "<product-number>",
 "Plant": "<receiving-plant>",
 "StorageLocation": "<storage-location>",
 "OrderQuantity": 1,
 "OrderQuantityUnit": "ST",
 "OrderQuantityUnitISOCode": "PCE",
 "NetPriceAmount": 60.00,
 "DocumentCurrency": "<currency>",
 "DeliveryDocumentType": "NCC3"
 }
 ]
} 
 Response (HTTP 201) — key fields: 
 Field Notes 
 StockTransportOrder Generated STO number 
 StockTransportOrderType Must be NBIC for 5HP 
 PurchasingInfoRecord Auto-resolved from master data 
 EffectiveAmount Net price + applicable tax 
 Five things that will break this call: 
 OrderQuantityUnitISOCode is required — omitting it returns "ISO unit must be provided" 
 StockTransportOrderItem must be a string ( "00010" ), not an integer ( 10 ) 
 Fetch the CSRF token in a separate preceding GET with header x-csrf-token: fetch 
 Write the JSON body to a file and use --data-binary @file — avoids PowerShell escape issues with nested quotes and special characters 
 API_PURCHASEORDER_PROCESS_SRV (OData V2) does not support NBIC STO document types — use the dedicated V4 service 
 Note: Account assignment at the item level is not supported for NBIC. The process is designed exclusively for stock-to-stock transfers between company codes. (→ KBA 3744416) 
 4. Step 2 — Create OBD ( ⚠️ Constraints for NBIC) 
 Service: API_OUTBOUND_DELIVERY_SRV (OData V2) 
 The standard API supports OBD creation via POST /A_OutbDeliveryHeader with ReferenceSDDocument pointing to the STO. However, for NBIC specifically, two prerequisites must be in place before this path is viable: 

 Value Chain Monitoring must be enabled for PO type NBIC. If value chains are not activated in the configuration activity Enable Value Chain Monitoring for Purchase Orders , OBD creation will fail at the backend. → KBA 3413153 

 Only a small set of fields is accepted on create. The API rejects any field not in the explicit allowlist: ReferenceSDDocument , ReferenceSDDocumentItem , ActualDeliveryQuantity , DeliveryQuantityUnit , ShippingPoint , DeliveryDocument , SerialNumber . All other fields must be set via a subsequent PATCH . → SAP Note 2899036 
 Alternative (tested in this flow): Application Job API — schedule a backend job to create OBDs in bulk against the STO. This is the SAP-recommended approach for high-volume scenarios and avoids the prerequisites and field constraints above. 
 Design rationale: For 5HP, OBD creation is a scheduled, bulk-oriented operation. Real-time per-STO OBD creation via REST is a secondary path and adds operational risk at scale. 
 5. Step 3 — OBD Picking and Goods Issue ( ✅ API Verified, curl Required) 
 The Session-Bound ETag Mechanism 
 All FunctionImport operations in API_OUTBOUND_DELIVERY_SRV require the CSRF token and ETag to be acquired within the same HTTP session as the subsequent POST. A stateless client that fetches a CSRF token and then calls PostGoodsIssue without session persistence will receive: 
 428 Precondition Required — no ETag provided 
 412 Precondition Failed — ETag is outdated or not seeded in the session 
 SAP Note 3539067 — Error when posting goods issue via API: 412 = ETag is outdated (re-GET the delivery and retry); 428 = ETag header is missing entirely. 
 Client Type Result Reason 
 Stateless (Postman, MCP, iFlow without session handler) 428 / 412 No shared session between CSRF fetch and POST 
 curl + cookie jar (same session) 200 ✅ CSRF fetch → entity GET → POST share one session 
 Correct call sequence: 
 $svcRoot = "https://<your-tenant>.s4hana.cloud.sap/sap/opu/odata/sap/API_OUTBOUND_DELIVERY_SRV"
$obd = "<outbound-delivery-number>"

# Step 0: Fetch CSRF token
# Important: target the entity set URL, NOT the service root
$fetchOut = & curl.exe -s -D - -o NUL `
 -u "${user}:${pass}" `
 -H "x-csrf-token: fetch" `
 -H "Accept: application/json" `
 -c $cookieJar `
 "$svcRoot/A_OutbDeliveryHeader"
$csrf = ($fetchOut | Select-String "(?i)x-csrf-token:\s*(.+)").Matches.Groups[1].Value.Trim()

# Step 1: GET entity in same session
# This seeds the ETag in the server-side session cache
& curl.exe -s -D - -o NUL `
 -u "${user}:${pass}" `
 -H "Accept: application/json" `
 -b $cookieJar -c $cookieJar `
 "$svcRoot/A_OutbDeliveryHeader('${obd}')?\`$format=json" 
 3a. PickAllItems — If-Match: not required 
 & curl.exe -s -X POST `
 -u "${user}:${pass}" `
 -H "x-csrf-token: $csrf" `
 -H "Accept: application/json" `
 -b $cookieJar -c $cookieJar `
 -w "`nHTTP:%{http_code}" `
 "$svcRoot/PickAllItems?DeliveryDocument='${obd}'&\`$format=json"
# Expected: HTTP 200 
 3b. ConfirmPickingAllItems — If-Match: do NOT include 
 & curl.exe -s -X POST `
 -u "${user}:${pass}" `
 -H "x-csrf-token: $csrf" `
 -H "Accept: application/json" `
 -b $cookieJar -c $cookieJar `
 -w "`nHTTP:%{http_code}" `
 "$svcRoot/ConfirmPickingAllItems?DeliveryDocument='${obd}'&\`$format=json"
# Expected: HTTP 200 
 Warning: Including If-Match in this call returns 412 unconditionally. This is not a configuration problem — the operation explicitly rejects the header. 
 3c. PostGoodsIssue — If-Match: * is mandatory 
 & curl.exe -s -X POST `
 -u "${user}:${pass}" `
 -H "x-csrf-token: $csrf" `
 -H "If-Match: *" `
 -H "Accept: application/json" `
 -b $cookieJar -c $cookieJar `
 -w "`nHTTP:%{http_code}" `
 "$svcRoot/PostGoodsIssue?DeliveryDocument='${obd}'&\`$format=json"
# Expected: HTTP 200, OverallGoodsMvtStatus = C 
 Material documents created after PGI (NBIC-specific): 
 Movement Type Plant Stock Change 
 MT681 Supplying plant Unrestricted → in-transit 
 MT107 (WL-linked) Receiving plant GR blocked stock +1 
 6. Step 4 — OBD Actual Posting Date ( ⚠️ Manual Step Required) 
 KBA 3794858 confirms that the Internal Actual Transfer of Control Date (Header → Shipping tab → Internal Transfer of Control Dates → Actual Date ) is not exposed as an updatable field in API_OUTBOUND_DELIVERY_SRV . After PGI, all header date fields are locked by the system. 
 Manual steps: 
 Open the OBD in Manage Outbound Deliveries (Fiori) or transaction VL02N 
 Header → Shipping tab → Internal Transfer of Control Dates 
 Set Actual Date to the current system date 
 Save 
 Why this is a blocker: The IBD PostGoodsReceipt FunctionImport validates this date as a precondition. Without it, the GR call will fail. 
 Enhancement path: If end-to-end automation of this date is required, raise an Enhancement Request referencing KBA 3794858 as the documented product limitation. 
 7. Step 5 — IBD Putaway Confirmation ( ✅ API Verified) 
 The IBD is auto-generated by the system immediately after PGI. Use API_INBOUND_DELIVERY_SRV for putaway. 
 $ibdRoot = "https://<your-tenant>.s4hana.cloud.sap/sap/opu/odata/sap/API_INBOUND_DELIVERY_SRV"
$ibd = "<inbound-delivery-number>" 
 Reuse the $csrf token and $cookieJar from Step 3 if still within the same session. If the session has expired, re-execute the CSRF fetch and entity GET sequence for the IBD service root. 
 5a. PutawayAllItems — If-Match: not required 
 & curl.exe -s -X POST `
 -u "${user}:${pass}" `
 -H "x-csrf-token: $csrf" `
 -H "Accept: application/json" `
 -b $cookieJar -c $cookieJar `
 "$ibdRoot/PutawayAllItems?DeliveryDocument='${ibd}'&\`$format=json" 
 5b. ConfirmPutawayAllItems — If-Match: not required 
 & curl.exe -s -X POST `
 -u "${user}:${pass}" `
 -H "x-csrf-token: $csrf" `
 -H "Accept: application/json" `
 -b $cookieJar -c $cookieJar `
 "$ibdRoot/ConfirmPutawayAllItems?DeliveryDocument='${ibd}'&\`$format=json" 
 8. Step 6 — Post Goods Receipt ( ✅ API Verified) 
 & curl.exe -s -X POST `
 -u "${user}:${pass}" `
 -H "x-csrf-token: $csrf" `
 -H "If-Match: *" `
 -H "Accept: application/json" `
 -b $cookieJar -c $cookieJar `
 "$ibdRoot/PostGoodsReceipt?DeliveryDocument='${ibd}'&\`$format=json"
# Expected: HTTP 200, OverallGoodsMovementStatus = C 
 Prerequisite: Step 4 (OBD Actual Posting Date) must be completed first. 
 Two-step material document movement unique to NBIC: 
 Movement Type Plant Stock Change Notes 
 MT107 (WL-linked) Receiving plant GR blocked +1 Linked to OBD — cannot be directly cancelled via MatDoc Cancel API (M7/492) 
 MT109 Receiving plant GR blocked -1 → unrestricted +1 Moves stock from restricted to unrestricted 
 MT107 being WL-linked to the OBD is expected NBIC behaviour, not an error. It does not indicate a problem with the preceding GI. 
 9. Step 7 — Intercompany Invoice IV2 (Auto-Generated, No Action Required) 
 After PGI, Output Determination automatically creates the IV2 intercompany invoice. No API call, job trigger, or manual action is needed. 
 Verify via query: 
 GET https://<your-tenant>.s4hana.cloud.sap/sap/opu/odata/sap/API_BILLING_DOCUMENT_SRV/A_BillingDocumentItem
 ?$filter=ReferenceSDDocument eq '<outbound-delivery-number>'
 &$select=BillingDocument,BillingDocumentItem,ReferenceSDDocument,
 Material,BillingQuantity,NetAmount
 &$format=json 
 Expected response — key fields: 
 Field Expected Value Notes 
 BillingDocumentType IV2 Intercompany invoice 
 CompanyCode Supplying company code Issuing entity 
 PartnerCompany Receiving company code Recipient entity 
 AccountingPostingStatus C FI document fully posted

items.title: SAP Joule for Developers: End of the Promotional Period and The Path Forward
items.author: steven_j
items.text:
SAP Joule for Developers, which brought generative AI capabilities into SAP Build and ABAP at no additional cost during its initial promotional period, is ending on September 30th, 2026. We are extending the promo offer for SAP Build features to December 31 st , 2026, and this post explains exactly what that means for you, what happens to each capability you may be using today, and what your path forward looks like after December 31 st , 2026. 
 We know changes like this require planning, and we want to give you as much clarity as possible, well in advance, so you can make informed decisions for your team and your projects. 
 What Does This Mean for You? 
 If you are using SAP Build generative AI capabilities today — SAP Build Process Automation generative AI features or Joule Studio, classic edition generative AI features — you retain full access through December 31, 2026. AI chat in SAP Build Code is already rolled out in Business Application Studio and will continue beyond December 31, 2026. SAP Joule for Developers, ABAP AI capabilities will be commercially available starting October 1, 2026, outside the promotion ( previously announced here ). 
 SAP Build continues as a customer-manag ed solut ion development platform for extending SAP applications. What is changing is the commercial structure behind certain AI capabilities that were offered on a promotional basis, and the transition of the SAP Joule for Developers brand that will only be associated with ABAP AI capabilities as we move into 2027. 
 Why Are We Making This Change? 
 SAP Joule for Developers promotional period was designed t o give customers hands-on experience with generative AI in SAP Build without an imme diat e commercial commitment. That exploration phase has provided real-world signal s on what delivers value. Based on customer feedback, we made deliberate decisions for each capability . W here usage and value are clear, we are moving capabilities into supported commercial models; where strategic alternatives exist to deliver better customer value, we are directing investment accordingly. 
 What Happens to Each Capability? 
 ABAP AI — Continues under commercial licensing 
 As announced in May 2026, ABAP AI moves to consumption-based pricing (PUPM model) effective October 1, 2026. If you are currently using ABAP AI under SAP Joule for Developers promotional access, SAP will contact you before the transition date with licensing details. More details available here . 
 Action required: Plan for a licensing transition before October 1, 2026. 
 AI assistance in SAP Build Code — Already Available in Business Application Studio 
 AI Chat in SAP Build Code has already been rolled out in Business Application Studio (BAS) for those using build-code (SAP Build Code) or build-default (SAP Build Developer) plans. This will remain available beyond December 31, 2026. No action is required from customers; your AI coding assistance experience is uninterrupted and enhanced to now allow you to configure your own large language model provider, such as SAP AI Core, a third party LLM provider, or Github Copilot. 
 SAP Build Process Automation GenAI features — Access through December 31, 2026 
 SAP Build customers using generative AI features in SAP Build Process Automation — including process generation, decision generation, form generation, script generation, and summarization — can continue using those features until December 31, 2026. items.title: Introducing AI-Assisted OCM Prompts in SAP Activate
items.author: ChristinaGalbreath
items.text:
Organizational Change Management (OCM) plays an important role in successful SAP implementations. Helping people understand, prepare for, and adopt new ways of working is essential to realizing the value of transformation. 
 To support project teams in these efforts, SAP Activate has introduced six new AI-Assisted prompts for OCM tasks , now available in all applicable SAP Activate roadmaps in the roadmap viewer . These prompts bring AI into key change management activities, helping teams structure their work, develop project deliverables, and prepare for important conversations with stakeholders. By accelerating preparation work and providing a structured starting point for key deliverables, the prompts can help teams work more efficiently and dedicate more time to reviewing outputs, engaging stakeholders, and addressing project-specific change management needs. 
 The new AI-Assisted prompts support change managers and project teams across several important areas of organizational change management such as: 
 Organizational Change Management Set-up 
 Establish the foundation for OCM activities by using AI assistance to help define the organizational change management structure, roles, and responsibilities needed to support the project. 
 Change Plan 
 Develop an initial change plan that helps organize change management activities, identify key considerations, and align change initiatives with project objectives and timelines. 
 Stakeholder Identification 
 Identify and organize key project stakeholders to help project teams understand who will be affected by the transformation and who should be involved throughout the project. 
 Stakeholder Engagement 
 Prepare stakeholder engagement activities that support meaningful participation, strengthen relationships, and help address stakeholder needs throughout the implementation. 
 Communication Plan 
 Develop an initial communication plan to help change managers structure communications, identify audiences, and plan relevant messages throughout the transformation. 
 Change Impact Workshop 
 Prepare for change impact workshops by organizing relevant project information to support the identification of potential impacts on business processes, roles and ways for work. 
 The new AI prompts are designed to help change managers and project teams get started with OCM deliverables and activities by providing structured guidance and AI-generated assistance. Depending on the task, teams can use the prompts to: 
 Organize project information and identify key considerations. 
 Develop initial drafts of change management deliverables. 
 Structure stakeholder identification and engagement activities. 
 Prepare for workshops and important project discussions. 
 Adapt AI-generated outputs to their specific project, organization, and solution. 
 By providing a starting point for these activities, AI-Assisted prompts can help teams focus their efforts on reviewing, refining, and applying the outputs to their project needs. AI assistance is a starting point, not a substitute for project expertise. Change managers and teams should review and validate generated content, incorporate relevant organizational knowledge, and tailor the results to their implementation context. 
 The introduction of AI-Assisted OCM prompts is another step in the evolution of SAP Activate, bringing AI capabilities closer to the activities project teams perform throughout their implementations. By combining the structured guidance of SAP Activate with AI-assisted content generation, change managers and project teams can explore new ways to approach change management planning and execution. 
 Explore the new AI-Assisted OCM prompts in the SAP Activate roadmap viewer and discover how they can support your next transformation project.

items.title: SAP ABAP Table Maintenance Generator (TMG) Events 1 to 5 – Complete Usage with Real-Time Examples
items.author: manijangiti
items.text:
Hi , In this blog, I’ll explain how to use SAP Table Maintenance Generator (TMG) Events 1 to 5 with simple, real-time examples. These TMG events help developers add custom logic during table maintenance in transaction SM30 — such as data checks, logging, or automatic updates. By understanding when each event is triggered, you can easily enhance the standard TMG behavior without changing SAP’s standard code. This post will take you through all five events step by step — explaining what each one does, when it runs, and how to use it in real projects. Event 01 – Before saving the data in the database Event 02 – After saving the data in the database Event 03 – Before deleting the displayed data Event 04 – After deleting the displayed data Event 05 – Creating a new entry Let’s start with how to create a Table Maintenance Generator (TMG) and the complete steps. AI-assisted tools were used to refine, structure, and enhance the clarity of the content presented in this blog. Step 1 : I have created a database table With some Fields . Step 2 : I have created a database table Log Entries For Event 04 . Step 3 : Let’s create a Table Maintenance Generator (TMG). Give The Function Group And Active the Function Group In SE80 T Code Step 4 : Now, create or modify events: go to Modification → Events and select the event names. Step 5 : Let’s start with Event 1, its use case, and an example code. Event 1 – Before Saving the Data in the Database. Use Case / Real-Time Example: Triggered before saving data in the database (Insert/Update). Automatically fills audit fields : CHANGEDBY = current user, CHANGEDON = current date. Ensures screen data ( extract ) and internal table ( total ) are updated before saving. Real-time example: In an employee table, when a record is updated, Event 1 automatically logs who changed it and when . Example Code : *----------------------------------------------------------------------* ***INCLUDE LZTAB_TMG_EVENTSF01. *----------------------------------------------------------------------* Form save. FIELD-SYMBOLS: TYPE any. LOOP AT total. CHECK EQ aendern. ASSIGN COMPONENT 'CHANGEDBY' OF STRUCTURE TO . IF sy-subrc = 0 . = sy-uname . ENDIF. ASSIGN COMPONENT 'CHANGEDON' OF STRUCTURE TO . IF sy-subrc = 0 . = sy-datum . ENDIF. READ TABLE extract WITH KEY . IF sy-subrc = 0. extract = total . MODIFY extract INDEX sy-tabix. ENDIF. MODIFY total. ENDLOOP. ENDFORM. When a user modifies a record, the system automatically updates the CHANGEDBY and CHANGEDON fields with the current user and date. Example Output: Step 6 : Let’s start with Event 2, its use case, and an example code. Event 2 –After Creating / Saving a Record. Use Case / Real-Time Example: Event 2 is triggered after a record is saved to the database. It is commonly used for post-processing , such as: Sending email notifications after new data is created. Triggering workflow or alerts for users. Logging audit or additional details after data insertion. Real-Time Example: In your ZTAB_TMG_EVENTS table, after a new employee record is created: An email is automatically sent to notify stakeholders. The email contains a formatted HTML table with all employee details ( EMPID , EMPNAME , CREATEDON , CREATEDBY , STATUS ). Example Code : *----------------------------------------------------------------------* ***INCLUDE LZTAB_TMG_EVENTSF03. *----------------------------------------------------------------------* form Email. DATA: lo_send_request TYPE REF TO cl_bcs, lo_document TYPE REF TO cl_document_bcs, lo_recipient TYPE REF TO if_recipient_bcs, lo_bcs_exception TYPE REF TO cx_bcs, lt_html_lines TYPE soli_tab, lv_html TYPE string, lv_subj TYPE so_obj_des, lv_sent TYPE abap_bool lv_email TYPE adr6-smtp_addr VALUE 'test@.com'. DATA: lt_events TYPE TABLE OF ztab_tmg_events, ls_event TYPE ztab_tmg_events. *---------------------------------------------------------------------* * 1️⃣ Read data from table *---------------------------------------------------------------------* SELECT * FROM ztab_tmg_events INTO TABLE _events. IF lt_events IS INITIAL. MESSAGE 'No data found in ZTAB_TMG_EVENTS' TYPE 'I'. EXIT. ENDIF. *---------------------------------------------------------------------* * 2️⃣ Build HTML Header *---------------------------------------------------------------------* CLEAR lt_html_lines. DATA: BODY TYPE STRING. BODY = 'Hi, Please find the table data After Creating'. CONCATENATE '' '

'BODY'

' '

Employee Data

' '' '' '' '' '' '' '' '' '' '' '' INTO lv_html. APPEND lv_html TO lt_html_lines. CLEAR lv_html. " Loop through data rows and add table rows dynamically LOOP AT lt_events INTO ls_event. CONCATENATE '' '' '' '' '' '' '' INTO lv_html. APPEND lv_html TO lt_html_lines. CLEAR lv_html. ENDLOOP. " Close table and HTML tags APPEND '
EMPIDEMPNAMECREATEDONCREATEDBYSTATUS
' ls_event-empid '' ls_event-empname '' ls_event-createdon '' ls_event-createdby '' ls_event-status '
' TO lt_html_lines. *---------------------------------------------------------------------* * 4️⃣ Send Email using CL_BCS *---------------------------------------------------------------------* TRY. lo_send_request = cl_bcs=>create_persistent( ). lv_subj = |ZTAB_TMG_EVENTS Report - { sy-datum DATE = USER }|. lo_document = cl_document_bcs=>create_document( i_type = 'HTM' i_text = lt_html_lines i_subject = lv_subj ). lo_send_request->set_document( lo_document ). lo_recipient = cl_cam_address_bcs=>create_internet_address( lv_email ). lo_send_request->add_recipient( lo_recipient ). lo_send_request->set_send_immediately( 'X' ). lv_sent = lo_send_request->send( ). IF lv_sent = abap_true. COMMIT WORK AND WAIT. MESSAGE |Email sent successfully to { lv_email }| TYPE 'S'. ELSE. MESSAGE 'Email sending failed' TYPE 'E'. ENDIF. CATCH cx_bcs INTO lo_bcs_exception. MESSAGE lo_bcs_exception->get_text( ) TYPE 'E'. ENDTRY. ENDFORM. Example Output: Step 6 : Event 3 – Before Deleting a Record Use Case / Real-Time Example: Event 3 is triggered before a record is deleted from the table. It is commonly used to: Validate records before deletion. Prevent deletion of critical or active records. Log information about records that are attempted to be deleted. Real-Time Example: In your ZCPY_TMG_EVENTS table, before deleting a record: The system checks if the record’s STATUS is 'A' (Active). If the record is active, deletion is blocked , and an error message is shown: "You cannot delete a record which is active." Only records that are not active can be deleted safely. Example Code : *---------------------------------------------------------------------* * Event 01: Before deleting the data displayed *---------------------------------------------------------------------* FORM del. DATA: lt_zcpy_tmg_events TYPE TABLE OF zcpy_tmg_events, ls_zcpy_tmg_events TYPE zcpy_tmg_events. "Collect records marked for deletion from TOTAL LOOP AT total. IF IS NOT INITIAL. "Correct system field for deletion mark MOVE-CORRESPONDING TO ls_zcpy_tmg_events. APPEND ls_zcpy_tmg_events TO lt_zcpy_tmg_events. CLEAR ls_zcpy_tmg_events. ENDIF. ENDLOOP. "Validate before deletion IF lt_zcpy_tmg_events IS NOT INITIAL. LOOP AT lt_zcpy_tmg_events INTO DATA(ls_imp). IF ls_imp-status = 'A'. "Assume 'A' = Active MESSAGE 'You cannot delete a record which is active.' TYPE 'E'. ENDIF. ENDLOOP. ENDIF. ENDFORM. Example Output : Step 7 : Event 4 – After Deleting the Displayed Data Use Case / Real-Time Example: Event 4 is triggered after records are deleted from the table. It is mainly used to: Log deleted records for audit purposes. Perform any post-deletion processing like notifications or updates in related tables. Real-Time Example: In your ZTAB_TMG_EVENTS table: When a record is deleted, the system stores information about the deleted record in a custom log table ZCPY_TMG_LOG . The log includes details like EMPID (key field), action performed ( DELETE ), user name, date, and time. This helps track who deleted what and when , which is critical for compliance and auditing. Example Code: *---------------------------------------------------------------------* * Event 04: After Deleting the Display Data *---------------------------------------------------------------------* FORM after_delete_data. FIELD-SYMBOLS: TYPE ztab_tmg_events, TYPE any. " Row of TOTAL table DATA: ls_deleted TYPE ztab_tmg_events, " Your TMG table structure ls_log TYPE zcpy_tmg_log, " Your custom log table lv_id TYPE zcpy_tmg_log-id. " Log ID LOOP AT total ASSIGNING . " Get the internal action flag for this record ASSIGN COMPONENT 'ACTION' OF STRUCTURE TO . " Check if this record was deleted IF = 'D'. " Cast generic to actual structure ASSIGN TO CASTING. " Now data is properly available ls_deleted = . " Get next log ID (better: use number range in real system) SELECT MAX( id ) INTO _id FROM zcpy_tmg_log. IF sy-subrc <> 0 OR lv_id IS INITIAL. lv_id = 1. ELSE. lv_id = lv_id + 1. ENDIF. " Fill log entry ls_log-id = lv_id. ls_log-tabname = 'ZTAB_TMG_EVENTS'. " Table name ls_log-keyfield = ls_deleted-empid. " Replace with your actual key field ls_log-action = 'DELETE'. ls_log-uuser = sy-uname. ls_log-ddate = sy-datum. ls_log-ttime = sy-uzeit. " Insert into log table INSERT zcpy_tmg_log FROM ls_log. CLEAR: ls_deleted, ls_log. ENDIF. ENDLOOP. ENDFORM. Example Output : Step 8 : Event 5 – Before Creating a New Record Use Case / Real-Time Example: Event 5 is triggered before a new record is saved in the table. It is mainly used to: Automatically assign key values (like Employee ID) to new records. Populate system fields like Created On and Created By . This ensures consistency and reduces manual errors when creating new entries. Real-Time Example: In your ZTAB_TMG_EVENTS table: When a user adds a new employee record, the system automatically generates a new EMPID based on the maximum existing ID. The fields CREATEDON and CREATEDBY are filled with the current date and the username of the person creating the record. This helps track who created the record and when, ensuring proper audit tracking. Example Code : *---------------------------------------------------------------------* ***INCLUDE LZTAB_TMG_EVENTSF02. *---------------------------------------------------------------------* FORM CREATE. DATA: LV_ID TYPE ZTAB_TMG_EVENTS-EMPID. " Get the maximum EMPID from the table SELECT MAX( EMPID ) INTO _ID FROM ZTAB_TMG_EVENTS. " Assign next EMPID IF LV_ID IS INITIAL. ZTAB_TMG_EVENTS-EMPID = 1. ELSE. ZTAB_TMG_EVENTS-EMPID = LV_ID + 1. ENDIF. " Populate system fields ZTAB_TMG_EVENTS-CREATEDON = SY-DATUM. ZTAB_TMG_EVENTS-CREATEDBY = SY-UNAME. ENDFORM. Thank You.....

While developing SAP Smart Forms, we sometimes need to display a subtotal for the line items printed on each page. This becomes challenging when the number of records that fit on a page is not equal to the total number of records. 
 For example, suppose a document contains 10 line items. If the Smart Form layout allows only 7 line items on the first page, the remaining 3 items will be printed on the next page. 
 The requirement is to calculate the netwr of the 7 records printed on the first page and display that amount as the page subtotal. On the next page, the remaining 3 records should have their own subtotal. In addition, a grand total can be displayed on the final page 
 Solution: 

 Step 1: Create the required global variables 
 Go to: 
 Smart Form → Global Settings → Global Definitions. 

 Create Footer Row for Page-Wise Subtotal. 

 Why use At page break only 
 The table can continue onto multiple pages. When Smart Forms reaches the end of the available space and moves the remaining records to the next page, the Footer row is triggered at the page break . 

 Clear the sub total variable after each page print. 

 For last page and final sub total and grand total . 

 Just for your reference : 

 example Output: 

 this is first page and there are total 20 pages for each page the sub total as printed . 

 Now lest see final page. 

 this is final page output which is grand total and sub total. 

 Key Points 
 The important points of this implementation are: 
 Maintain a separate variable for the page subtotal . 
 Maintain another variable for the grand total . 
 Add every line item's NETWR to both variables. 
 Use At page break only to print the subtotal when a page ends. 
 Clear only the page subtotal after it has been printed. 
 Do not clear the grand total during page processing. 
 Handle the final page separately because it does not have a subsequent page break. 
 Display the final-page subtotal and grand total together on the last page. 

 Conclusion 
 Displaying page-wise subtotals in SAP Smart Forms can be challenging when a table spans multiple pages because the number of records printed on each page is determined by the available layout space. 
 By maintaining separate page subtotal and grand total variables and using the appropriate Smart Forms table events, we can achieve the required output:

 The blog explains the approach for page-wise subtotals and displaying the grand total on the final page.

items.title: Unable to put a SFC on hold using Manage Holds app in SAP Digital Manufacturing
items.author: khyou99
items.text:
We are currently configuring and testing SAP Digital Manufacturing (SAP DM) for process manufacturing workflows (using process orders and master recipes) and have hit a configuration roadblock regarding SFC holds, Order POD visibility, and sequence flexibility. 
 We are trying to achieve three key requirements simultaneously, but system constraints seem to conflict with each other. Here is what we are experiencing: 
 1. The Starting Constraint (SFC Holds) 
 Per SAP Note 3379404 , the system blocks the "Hold" functionality if both Material Autocomplete and Confirm is set to 'No' and Quantity Validation is set to 'No' . To use the Manage Holds app, we are forced to change one of these settings to Yes . 
 However, both options introduce major hurdles for our process industry workflow: 
 Dilemma A: Setting "Material Autocomplete and Confirm = Yes" 

 The Problem: Once we enable this flag in the Manage Materials app, all SFCs related to the material completely disappear from the Order POD across all statuses (not just completed ones). 

 Impact: This is a non-starter for us because operators lose all visibility of active SFCs in the Order POD. 
 Dilemma B: Setting "Quantity Validation = Yes" 

 The Problem: When we set Quantity Validation to Yes in the recipe/routing to satisfy the hold requirement, the system enforces strict sequence gating. Operators are blocked from starting a subsequent phase or operation before the previous one is fully completed. 
 Impact: Our business requirement demands operational flexibility—operators need the ability to start/execute certain phases or operations out of sequence. 
 Our Core Question: 
 How can we achieve a working solution in SAP DM process manufacturing that allows us to: 

 Put SFCs on hold using the Manage Holds app (complying with SAP Note 3379404 ). 

 Maintain full visibility of SFCs in the Order POD (meaning Autocomplete and Confirm must likely stay No ). 

 Retain the flexibility to execute or start operations/phases out of sequence without being blocked by strict quantity/sequence gating in a master recipe framework? 
 Has anyone encountered this specific triad of requirements in process industries, and what is the recommended best practice or workaround? 
 Thank you in advance for your insights!
